- **Unless its role opts in, a resident agent keeps only the tools a reviewed classification says write no file and run no command (bob#213).** Every tool an agent's allowlist can name (pi's built-ins and every tool a blessed capability's manifest declares) has a reviewed row in `TOOL_EFFECTS` (`src/shell/tool-allowlist.ts`): `read-only`, `writer` (writes a file the model names, or runs a command), `effect` (a memory write, a Discord post or reaction, a status report, a robot action, cancelling a job this run started) or `egress` (a web tool that sends model-influenced data outside the office; a resident agent drops it unless its role sets `tools.allowResidentWeb`, which the shell opt-in does not cover). `RESIDENT_EXCLUDED_TOOLS` is derived from it: every `writer`, plus any declared name without a row. It now includes anchored-edit's `write_file`, `edit_lines` and `insert_after` beside `bash`, `write`, `edit`, `powershell` and `run`, so a resident agent without its role's `allowResidentShell` opt-in no longer keeps them. A role that sets `tools.allowResidentShell: true` keeps its writers for a resident agent (the agent's `bob.yaml` can turn that off, not on); builder-local, the one shipped role that lists the anchored-edit writers, opts in, and so does coder. A test enumerates the manifests' tools and fails on a name without a row, and on a row no manifest or pi built-in provides. (`test/shell/tool-allowlist.test.ts`)
